summary.business_type: SaaS / developer tool (free MIT Chrome DevTools extension, no signup)
top_findings: aggregateRating (5.0, n=7) injected sitewide in layout.tsx:109-115 with no visible rating content on any page: structured-data policy risk
Render-blocking Google Fonts stylesheet costs a measured 907-1050ms on every page to style two labels in one button; drives homepage LCP to 4.38s
No og:image on any inner page: pages overriding openGraph without images drop the root file-convention image, so /vs/ shares with no preview
No security headers beyond HSTS on any route (no CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, X-Frame-Options)
No page targets 'edit indexeddb chrome devtools', whose SERP is entirely workarounds for the limitation this product removes
quick_wins: Move Google Sans to next/font/google: one file, recovers roughly 1s of LCP
Delete the aggregateRating block: one deletion removes the only manual-action risk
Add twitter + openGraph.images to the 4 page metadata exports missing them: one pass fixes three reported symptoms
Add security headers via next.config.ts headers(): one block
Add contextual internal links from /vs/ and the query post to the homepage: two hrefs
data_limitations: No Google API credentials: no CrUX field data, no Search Console indexation or query data, no GA4. All performance numbers are Lighthouse lab.
Backlinks limited to Common Crawl plus a link verifier: no DA/PA, no spam scoring, no discovery of unknown inbound links.
4 of 8 target queries SERP-checked; 4 not checked.
Performance measured on 3 of 9 URLs; desktop strategy not measured.

categories.name: Technical SEO
what_works: Fully server-rendered on every URL (is_spa false)
Valid robots.txt declaring sitemap, open to all crawlers
Canonicals match sitemap entries
HTTPS with HSTS max-age 63072000
Correct mobile viewport, no horizontal overflow at 390px
No hreflang needed for single-market site
Sitemap covers all 9 live pages, valid XML, no orphans

findings.title: No CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy or X-Frame-Options on any route
findings.description: Verified via curl -D- on /, /privacy/, /blog/ and the 404 page: only strict-transport-security is present.
findings.recommendation: Add all four via next.config.ts headers(). Falsifiable: curl -D- must show them post-deploy. Gate it in CI.

findings.title: /privacy/ inherits homepage OG wholesale including wrong og:url
findings.description: src/app/privacy/page.tsx defines no openGraph or twitter metadata, so og:url renders as https://idxbeaver.portlabs.in/ instead of /privacy/.
findings.recommendation: Add openGraph + twitter blocks with url /privacy/. Ship with the twitter merge fix, same root cause.

findings.title: twitter:* metadata wrong on /blog/, /faq/, /about/
findings.description: These pages override metadata.openGraph but never metadata.twitter. Next.js merges per top-level key, so the root layout's whole twitter object is inherited. Confirmed: /faq/ og:title is page-correct while twitter:title is the homepage's.
findings.recommendation: Add a twitter block mirroring openGraph on each, the pattern /vs/ and the blog posts already use correctly.

findings.title: Six internal hrefs lack trailing slashes, forcing avoidable 308s
findings.description: site-footer.tsx, site-nav.tsx:142, faq/page.tsx:182 and :229, blog-post.tsx:53, blog/debugging-indexeddb-in-chrome-devtools/page.tsx:174. next.config.ts trailingSlash true means each 308-redirects.
findings.recommendation: Append trailing slashes. Falsifiable: grep -rn 'href="/[a-z-]*"' src returns zero excluding bare /.

findings.title: Render-blocking Google Fonts stylesheet loaded sitewide
findings.description: layout.tsx:77-81 adds preconnect, preload and a blocking stylesheet for Google Sans, used only in cws-install-button.tsx:4. See Performance for the measured cost.
findings.recommendation: Move to next/font/google or drop the brand font for that button.

findings.title: Two titles over 60 chars, one meta description at 218 chars
findings.description: /blog/debugging-indexeddb-in-chrome-devtools/ title 72 chars; /blog/browser-storage-quotas-explained/ title 89 chars and description 218 chars.
findings.recommendation: Shorten below ~60 and ~160 respectively, keeping the lead keyword phrase.

findings.title: /changelog/ and /docs/ 404s are not defects
findings.description: Both strings appear only in src/lib/demo-seed.ts:47-48 as fixture route names for the extension's own IndexedDB demo data. Nothing on the site links to them.
findings.recommendation: No action. Monitor 404 hit rate only if external links to these paths appear.

categories.name: Content Quality
what_works: Zero-telemetry claim verified true: no fetch, XHR or analytics in extension source, no remote endpoints in manifest
Privacy page permission list matches manifest exactly
MIT license and SQL/ZIP export claims verified against LICENSE and export.ts/import.ts
E-E-A-T: Experience 85, Expertise 80, Trustworthiness 85
Readability appropriate for a developer audience

findings.title: All three blog posts fall well short of the word floor for their type
findings.description: Posts measure 641-777 words against a 1,500-word floor, 40-65% of target, while framed as practical guides.
findings.recommendation: Add worked examples, edge cases and troubleshooting to close coverage gaps. Do not pad to a number.

findings.title: sitemap.ts stamps build-time lastmod on 6 of 9 pages
findings.description: sitemap.ts:16 sets const lastModified = new Date() once and reuses it for /, /vs/, /blog/, /faq/, /about/, /privacy/. Only blog posts use real dates. /privacy/ shows users 'Last updated 2026-04-27' while the sitemap claims the build time.
findings.recommendation: Use a per-route date, the pattern the blog posts already follow. Falsifiable: change one page, only its lastmod should move.

findings.title: JSON-LD dateModified hardcoded equal to datePublished
findings.description: The /vs/ page and blog-post.tsx set dateModified = datePublished statically, so real edits never register.
findings.recommendation: Derive both from the same per-route constant as the sitemap fix.

findings.title: Batch-publish pattern with no subsequent revision
findings.description: /vs/ and all three posts share a 2026-04-29 date, five days after launch, and dateModified has never moved.
findings.recommendation: Stagger future posts and make genuinely dated revisions.

findings.title: Authoritativeness is the weak E-E-A-T axis
findings.description: Scored 55 of 100. Solo author, no external validation, no third-party citations or named adopters surfaced on-page.
findings.recommendation: Address via the backlink and off-site plan rather than on-page copy.

findings.title: Legacy keywords meta array present
findings.description: Inert for ranking purposes, hygiene only.
findings.recommendation: Drop it.

categories.name: On-Page SEO
what_works: Titles and meta descriptions unique per page
Single H1 per page with sensible hierarchy
Canonicals correct and matching sitemap
Keyword targeting sensible per page
Sitemap covers all 9 live pages with no orphans

findings.title: Internal linking depth is thin on key pages
findings.description: /vs/ and the query post each contain exactly one href, an external GitHub link. Neither links to the homepage or a topical sibling.
findings.recommendation: Add a body link to / and one sibling on each. Two hrefs, and it makes later content investment compound.

findings.title: Home, /vs/ and /faq/ overlap not fully assessed
findings.description: The duplication check did not complete within the pass. Neither confirmed nor ruled out.
findings.recommendation: Re-run a duplicate-content pass before treating overlap as a known issue.

findings.title: Correction: the earlier 'sitemap omits /privacy/' claim was wrong
findings.description: This audit's initial recon used a truncated fetch that cut the 9th sitemap entry. The live sitemap contains all 9 URLs including /privacy/, confirmed by direct count, and sitemap.ts:35 includes it. A 10-point deduction based on this was removed, raising this category from 72 to 82.
findings.recommendation: No action. Recorded so a future pass does not re-flag it.

categories.name: Schema / Structured Data
what_works: No deprecated or banned types present (no HowTo, SpecialAnnouncement, CourseInfo, EstimatedSalary)
SoftwareApplication is otherwise well specified: applicationCategory, operatingSystem, browserRequirements, offers price 0, license, softwareHelp
BreadcrumbList present
BlogPosting blocks carry author with url

findings.title: aggregateRating sitewide with no visible rating content on any page
findings.description: layout.tsx:109-115 injects ratingValue 5, ratingCount 7 into the SoftwareApplication JSON-LD on every page. Confirmed live in rendered HTML. No page renders any rating, review or testimonial; the only 'review' strings in the HTML are demo-grid fixture data. The source comment at :106-108 says the values come from the Chrome Web Store and warns about staleness, but the problem is more basic: Google requires rating markup to reflect rating content visible on the page carrying it.
findings.recommendation: Delete the block, or render the Chrome Web Store rating on-page with a visible link to its source and then keep it. Falsifiable: if aggregateRating is in the JSON-LD, a visible sourced rating must be in the rendered body.

findings.title: All four Article/BlogPosting blocks missing required image
findings.description: None of the four blocks include image, and no per-post opengraph-image route exists. image is required for Article rich-result eligibility.
findings.recommendation: Point at the root opengraph-image as a stopgap, then build per-post routes. Shares a root cause with the missing og:image finding.

findings.title: No WebSite entity and no @id graph
findings.description: No WebSite type anywhere. SoftwareApplication, Article/BlogPosting, Person, the Organization stub and BreadcrumbList are all disconnected inline objects with no @id, so nothing identifies them as the same entities across pages.
findings.recommendation: Add a WebSite entity (no potentialAction, there is no site search) and @id every Person, Organization and WebSite mention, referencing by @id.

findings.title: publisher is a bare Organization stub
findings.description: publisher on all four content blocks is only {'@type':'Organization','name':'IdxBeaver'}, with no url, logo or sameAs. src/app/icon.png already exists and is unused for this.
findings.recommendation: Define Organization once with url, logo, sameAs to GitHub and the Chrome Web Store, and an @id referenced from every publisher field.

findings.title: BreadcrumbList item URLs lack trailing slashes
findings.description: Items point at non-canonical URLs that 308-redirect. Root cause is each page's alternates.canonical omitting the slash; correctness today depends implicitly on next.config.ts trailingSlash true.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit trailing slashes to canonicals and breadcrumb item URLs.

findings.title: author.url inconsistent between blocks
findings.description: The three BlogPosting blocks include author.url; the /vs/ Article omits it.
findings.recommendation: Reference one Person @id from every author field so it cannot drift.

findings.title: FAQPage present on /faq/
findings.description: Valid FAQPage JSON-LD with authored product Q&A. Google retired FAQ rich results for all sites on 2026-05-07, so it has no SERP benefit, and any AI citation benefit is unconfirmed. Correctly typed: it is authored product FAQ, not user-submitted, so QAPage does not apply.
findings.recommendation: No action. Do not remove, and do not add new FAQPage for SERP benefit.

categories.name: Performance (CWV)
what_works: CLS is 0 on all three measured pages
TBT 19.5ms / 10.5ms / 0ms, far under the 200ms threshold
TTFB 56-186ms, all good
Body font correctly self-hosted via next/font
Images already ship AVIF

findings.title: Render-blocking font is the dominant LCP cost
findings.description: Measured render-blocking cost 965ms on /, 907ms on /vs/, 1050ms on the blog post, from the fonts.googleapis.com stylesheet in layout.tsx. Used only for two labels in cws-install-button.tsx.
findings.recommendation: Move to next/font/google. Falsifiable: no fonts.googleapis.com link in raw HTML and homepage LCP below ~3.4s on re-measure.

findings.title: LCP fails good on the homepage and misses on inner pages
findings.description: Lighthouse mobile lab: / 4.38s (poor), /vs/ 3.42s, blog post 2.94s, all text LCP elements. Element render delay measured at 1195ms / 1495ms / 539ms. With CLS 0 and TBT under 20ms, the deficit is isolated to render-blocking resources.
findings.recommendation: Fix the font first; everything else is small by comparison. No CrUX baseline exists, so compare against this audit's lab run.

findings.title: Hero screenshot oversampled about 8x its display size
findings.description: dark.avif served at 2940x1728 into a 370x217 box; 71.1KB of 72.3KB measured as waste. Already AVIF and not the LCP element.
findings.recommendation: Add responsive sizes/srcset, or next/image with a sizes prop.

findings.title: Nav logo ships an oversized PNG on every page
findings.description: logo-mark-128.png is 21.5KB served at 128x128 and displayed at 28x28. Loads sitewide via the shared nav.
findings.recommendation: Convert to SVG, or export a correctly sized WebP/AVIF.

findings.title: 14KB of unnecessary core-js polyfills
findings.description: Array.prototype.at/flat/flatMap and Object.fromEntries shims ship on all three measured pages, all natively supported by Next.js's default browser target.
findings.recommendation: Check for a browserslist or build-target override. Low priority given TBT is near zero.

findings.title: Six of nine URLs and desktop strategy not measured
findings.description: /blog/, two of three posts, /faq/, /about/ and /privacy/ were not measured, nor was desktop.
findings.recommendation: Treat inner-page numbers as representative, not complete.

categories.name: AI Search Readiness
what_works: robots.txt returns byte-identical 200s for GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, CCBot, Applebot-Extended and anthropic-ai, with no CDN or WAF cloaking
Every URL fully server-rendered, so no JS-dependency for AI crawlers
llms.txt present, detailed and accurate against both the live product and the repo
FAQ, /vs/ and blog content genuinely well shaped for direct-answer extraction

findings.title: No Organization entity and no Wikidata or Wikipedia anchor for the brand
findings.description: publisher is a bare name string; no Organization with sameAs, logo or url exists anywhere, so 'IdxBeaver' is not defined as a machine-readable entity.
findings.recommendation: Add the Organization entity with sameAs to GitHub and the Chrome Web Store. Same fix as the schema finding.

findings.title: Sitewide AggregateRating has no on-page corroboration
findings.description: Every page asserts a 5.0 rating from 7 ratings with no visible source, which is a citability liability as well as a policy one.
findings.recommendation: Surface the source on-page or drop the markup.

findings.title: No confirmed Reddit or YouTube presence
findings.description: These are the strongest citation-correlated off-site surfaces for developer tools. Neither was found in the checks available this pass, and no search tool was available to the specialist to confirm.
findings.recommendation: Publish one short demo video and one genuine subreddit contribution tied to a real milestone. Falsifiable by direct search for the brand name.

findings.title: /about/ leads with narrative before any direct definition
findings.description: The crisp definition, that IdxBeaver is a Chrome DevTools extension turning the Application panel into a real database client, exists only on /faq/. That is the sentence an AI engine would lift.
findings.recommendation: Move a one-sentence definition to the top of /about/ and the homepage.

findings.title: No RSL 1.0 licensing declaration
findings.description: /rsl.xml and /.well-known/rsl.xml both 404; licensing is stated in prose only, though the product is already MIT.
findings.recommendation: Add a minimal RSL file. Falsifiable: 200 with valid syntax at /rsl.xml.

categories.name: Images
what_works: Full AVIF/WebP/PNG fallback chain on product images
Descriptive, appropriate alt text throughout
Explicit width and height on every image
Homepage above-the-fold solid at both 1440px and 390px, no horizontal overflow

findings.title: No og:image on any inner page
findings.description: Verified live: / renders og:image, while /vs/chrome-devtools-application-panel/, /faq/ and /blog/debugging-indexeddb-in-chrome-devtools/ render neither og:image nor twitter:image. Any page setting its own openGraph block without images drops the root file-convention image. /vs/, the high-intent comparison page, shares with no preview image at all.
findings.recommendation: Add openGraph.images to every page that overrides openGraph, then build per-page images. Falsifiable: all 9 URLs must render a non-empty og:image.

findings.title: No install CTA above the fold on /vs/ at 390px
findings.description: The mobile fold shows H1, intro and the start of the comparison table, with only an unopened hamburger. This is the page most likely to catch high-intent comparison traffic.
findings.recommendation: Add a compact or sticky install CTA above or beside the comparison table.

findings.title: /vs/ and blog pages contain no product screenshots at all
findings.description: All five images on /vs/ are brand logo and icon assets. An evaluator has to leave the page to see what the tool looks like. All three blog posts contain zero images.
findings.recommendation: Embed the existing dark/light screenshots on /vs/ and at least one visual per post.

findings.title: Product screenshots eager-loaded despite sitting far below the fold
findings.description: compare-slider.tsx dark.png/light.png have no loading attribute and one carries fetchPriority high, yet they render roughly 900px below the homepage fold. Neither is the LCP element.
findings.recommendation: Add loading lazy and drop fetchPriority high.

findings.title: Product screenshots about 3x oversized for rendered width
findings.description: Intrinsic 2940x1728 against a rendered width of roughly 900-940px CSS, with no srcset or sizes. The WebP fallback is 220KB and the PNG fallback 708KB.
findings.recommendation: Add responsive srcset/sizes or switch to next/image with a sizes prop.

findings.title: Hero logo alt text unreachable to assistive tech
findings.description: hero.tsx img carries alt 'IdxBeaver' but its parent div has aria-hidden true, stripping it from the accessibility tree. Other logo instances correctly use empty alt as decorative.
findings.recommendation: Remove aria-hidden from the wrapper, or set this instance's alt empty for consistency.

findings.title: Orphaned unused image assets
findings.description: public/screenshots/query.{png,webp,avif} exist on disk at 48-436KB with no reference anywhere in src/. The nav has a Query link with no corresponding section.
findings.recommendation: Wire them into a Query feature section, or delete them.

phases.name: Phase 1: Critical Fixes
items: Remove or substantiate the aggregateRating block in layout.tsx:109-115
Self-host Google Sans via next/font/google, replacing the render-blocking stylesheet in layout.tsx:77-81

phases.name: Phase 2: High-Impact Improvements
items: Fix the Next.js metadata merge bug in one pass: add twitter blocks and openGraph.images to the 4 pages missing them, and give /privacy/ its own blocks
Add CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy and X-Frame-Options via next.config.ts headers()
Add image to all four Article/BlogPosting schema blocks
Add contextual internal links from /vs/ and the query post to the homepage and a sibling
Fix the 6 non-canonical internal hrefs and the BreadcrumbList item URLs

phases.name: Phase 3: Content & Authority
items: Write the page targeting 'edit indexeddb chrome devtools', the highest-value content gap found
Re-angle the query post to lead with the native IndexedDB API before the Mongo-style layer
Deepen all three blog posts from 641-777 words and add at least one visual each
Ship the export post, then a single consolidated storage-types post
Fix lastmod in sitemap.ts:16 and derive dateModified from the same per-route constant
Add an install CTA and product screenshots to /vs/
Add Organization and WebSite entities with @id linking
Earn the first independent backlinks: awesome-lists and roundups, then StackOverflow answers

phases.name: Phase 4: Monitoring & Iteration
items: Verify Search Console and add a CrUX/PageSpeed API key to replace lab data with field data
Diff each deploy against the drift baselines captured 2026-09-09 for /, /vs/ and /faq/

Batch the remaining small items: title and description lengths, image sizing, lazy-loading, hero alt, orphaned assets, product definition placement, blog secondary CTA, inert keywords and changefreq/priority, browserslist polyfills
